During pendency of the suit the defendant filed an application under Order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint stating, inter alia, that the plaintiff has no cause of action for the suit and as per statements made in the plaint the  plaintiffs suit was hopelessly barred by limitation. 

 12. It may further be stated here that under section 21 of the Civil Courts Act an appeal from a decree or order of the Subordinate Judge shall lie to the District Judge where the value of the original suit did not exceed Taka 1,30,000.00 and to the High Court Division in any other case but the Artha Rin Adalat Ain provides that an appeal against the decree or order of the Artha Rin Adalat shall lie to the High Court irrespective of the value of the suit. It further appears that under section 7 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain an appeal is to be filed within 30 days from that date of judgment or order to the High Court but the period of limitation for preferring regular appeal is 90 days. From our above discussion it is quite clear that the Artha Rin Adalat is not an ordinary Civil Court but Special Civil Court created by special law for limited purpose.
